questions.question: What is your favourite food?
correctAnswers: Something simple done really well—good bread, ripe tomatoes, olive oil—the sort of food that doesn’t need to prove anything.
Whatever tastes like home in that moment; sometimes it’s comfort food, sometimes it’s something completely new.
I tend to love food that feels unpretentious but thoughtful, the kind you remember long after the meal is over.
Probably something warm and familiar that reminds me of good company and an unhurried evening.
It changes often, but I always gravitate toward food that feels honest and carefully made.
incorrectAnswers: There’s this pasta dish that my mother makes. Nothing compares to a home cooked meal.
I can’t decide, but probably something my grandma cooks.
Something innovative and daring that blends bold flavours with cross-cultural ingredients.
The appetiser bread at my favourite childhood French restaurant.

questions.question: When was the last time you felt alive?
correctAnswers: A few weeks ago I was walking home late at night after finishing something difficult—it was quiet and I realised how good it felt to finally be done.
The last time I stayed up too late working on a project and suddenly noticed it was 3 a.m. and I hadn’t checked the time once.
Recently, standing somewhere high up with a view of the city just as the lights were coming on.
The moment right after trying something I wasn’t sure I could pull off and realising it actually worked.
Not long ago during a long walk where the weather was perfect and everything felt strangely clear.
incorrectAnswers: My friends and I decided that 4am was too late to go to sleep, so we stayed up and watched the sunset on the beach. It was beautiful.
I was jamming with my best friends on a random Saturday afternoon. Probably that.
Watching my home city’s football team score the winning point and celebrating with everyone in the stadium.

questions.question: What are you most looking forward to?
correctAnswers: Finishing a long stretch of work and finally having a quiet week where I can slow down a bit.
Seeing where the projects I’m currently building actually end up a few years from now.
Travelling somewhere new again and getting that first-day feeling of not quite knowing the place yet.
The moment when something I’ve been working on privately is finally ready to show people.
The next phase where a lot of small efforts start turning into something tangible.
incorrectAnswers: The prospect of continuing to live in the city long enough to call it home.
A mid-summer trip to Spain with my friends.
Falling in love and being loved.

questions.question: Who inspires you?
correctAnswers: A professor I had who treated every question seriously and somehow made difficult ideas feel exciting.
Friends who quietly build interesting things without making a spectacle of it.
A filmmaker I once heard speak who talked more about patience than talent.
People who keep working at something for years even when no one is paying attention yet.
Anyone who manages to stay curious about the world long after school or training ends.
incorrectAnswers: My eighty-something-year-old professor who somehow has more energy than I do and approaches the subject with such nuance and care.
My parents who worked tirelessly to support their children.
People who work diligently and share their passions with the world.

questions.question: Where do you feel most comfortable?
correctAnswers: At a desk late at night when everything is quiet and I can finally focus.
In small cafés where people are talking softly and no one is rushing you out the door.
Walking through a familiar part of the city where I know exactly where everything is.
In rooms where people are discussing ideas rather than trying to impress each other.
Anywhere that feels calm enough to think but alive enough to feel interesting.
incorrectAnswers: Curled up at my desk in sweatpants doing something creative after a long day.
On a cozy couch reading a book on a rainy day.
On a rooftop at night chatting and laughing with my friends.
Basking in the sun on a lazy Sunday morning.

questions.question: How do your friends perceive you?
correctAnswers: Probably as the person who overthinks things but is usually the one organising plans.
Someone who listens a lot and then eventually offers a very specific opinion.
A bit intense about projects but fairly relaxed about everything else.
The friend who asks too many questions but means well.
Someone dependable who also disappears occasionally when working on something.
incorrectAnswers: Hopefully as a compassionate person who strives to be honest.
A hot-headed but ultimately caring person.
A good listener who sometimes talks too much.
A seemingly cold but dedicated and kind person.

questions.question: Are you lonely?
correctAnswers: Not really, though there are moments—like walking home late—when you wish someone else had been there for the conversation.
Occasionally, especially during busy periods when everyone’s schedules stop lining up.
Sometimes, but it usually fades once I spend an evening with friends or get back into something meaningful.
In small, passing ways rather than anything heavy or constant.
Not often—solitude and loneliness feel different once you get used to working on your own.
incorrectAnswers: Sometimes I feel very lonely, other times I feel like I belong—it really depends on the situation, I don’t know.
Yes, especially now that I’m in a new place with new people.
Yes—but I quite like my own company, it’s calming.
No. I feel loved and cared for. I’m not lonely at all.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself in five years?
correctAnswers: Hopefully somewhere that reflects a lot of hard work I’m putting in now.
Running or building something that started as a small idea on a laptop.
In a place where the projects I care about have matured into something real.
Still learning, but with a clearer sense of direction than I have today.
Ideally in a role where I can look back at the last few years and feel they were spent building something worthwhile.
incorrectAnswers: Doing better than I am now and at a place where I can look back and laugh at all the things I was worried about.
Working abroad in a new country, exploring new places and meeting new people.
Making things no matter what, but hopefully bigger and better than anything right now.
I’m not sure... But I’m excited to explore what the future holds.
